items.title: [Feature]: sm120 Cake MegaMoE for PCIe hosts: MXFP4-activation (W4A4) variant, int8/FP8 return codec, switch-level dedupe
items.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

On PCIe-only sm_120 hosts (8 GPUs behind two PCIe Gen5 switches, no NVLink; ~49-55 GB/s per direction on the x16 links and on the inter-switch fabric) `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake` is slower per MoE layer than an unfused DeepEP-style all-to-all + DeepGEMM grouped-GEMM path, because its wire format carries roughly twice the bytes:

- dispatch records carry FP8 activations: 5120 + 160 (+224 header) B per row at H=5120, where an MXFP4 dispatch carries 2560 + 160 B;
- expert results return through the lossless BF16 codec, ~7.8 KB per route, where an int8 combine (per-128 fp32 scale) carries 5.3 KB;
- records are deduplicated per destination rank only; on a two-switch host, one copy per destination switch with the partial sums reduced inside the switch before crossing sends 2.2x fewer cross-switch bytes at EP8.

Measured at the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash routed geometry (E=384, H=5120, I=2304, top-k 6; EP8, 2048 tokens/rank, 6-layer CUDA graph, slowest rank, us/layer; the local-memory guard was raised to 16 B so the kernel loads at this geometry, see #6755):

| path | uniform | hot (one rank 2.5x) | recorded routing |
|---|---|---|---|
| unfused: all-to-all (one copy per destination switch, in-switch partial-sum reduction) + DeepGEMM grouped GEMM, **MXFP4 activations, int8 combine** | 3850 | 6243 | 4390 |
| same unfused path with **FP8 activations** (per-128 fp32 scales), int8 combine | 5623 | 9449 | 6447 |
| cake, `transport_table` = LSA inside each switch / GIN across (explicit table) | 4745-4936 (two runs) | 7478 | 5677 |
| cake `all_gin` / `all_lsa` | 6067 / 6050 | 7718 / 7615 | 7632 / 6247 |

Against the same-precision unfused path the fused kernel is 14-26% faster, so the overlap works; against the MXFP4-activation path it is 20-28% slower. Switching only the unfused path's activations from MXFP4 to FP8 moves its dispatch from 692 to 1328 us/layer (per-card egress 23.9 -> 46.4 MB/layer), so on these links bytes are time. Numerics for reference (rel L2 vs an fp32 reference with unquantized activations, 512 rows/rank): cake 4.7%, FP8-activation unfused path 4.8%, MXFP4-activation path 22%; cake vs the kernel-boundary oracle of `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_sm120_w4a8_cake_mega.py` 1.6e-4 .. 3.2e-4.

### Requested outcome

A configuration of the sm120 Cake MegaMoE whose bytes on the wire match the unfused W4A4 path on PCIe hosts:

1. an MXFP4-activation variant (e2m1 + UE8M0 per-32 scales, `mma.sync kind::mxf4nvf4`): dispatch rows become 2560 + 160 B and both GEMMs run at the FP4 rate instead of the FP8 rate;
2. an int8 (per-128 fp32 scale) or FP8 return option in place of the lossless BF16 codec, selectable per deployment, with the combine summing the dequantized partials;
3. optionally, topology-aware dedupe in the transport table: one copy per destination LSA group (PCIe switch or host) with in-group fan-out on dispatch and in-group partial-sum reduction on return.

(1) + (2) alone remove the byte handicap, which is the whole 20-28% gap in the table above; what remains after that is the overlap efficiency of the protocol on PCIe (in these runs the kernel hides about a third of the communication time). The kernel's numerics already match the unfused FP8 path, so the request is about the transport format, not a new precision recipe.

### Target hardware

SM120 (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 50-series)

### Inference engine

vLLM

### Affected model or model family

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4 routed experts: E=384, H=5120, I=2304, top-k 6, 1 shared expert)

### Workload and configuration

- Data type and quantization: MXFP4 expert weights (e2m1 + UE8M0 per-32) from the checkpoint; activations MXFP4 in our production path, FP8 (per-128 fp32 scale) in the same-precision control and FP8 (UE8M0 per-32) inside Cake; int8 combine (per-128 fp32 scale) on the unfused path, lossless BF16 codec in Cake
- Batch size or request concurrency: prefill, 2048 tokens per rank per step (also 384 and 1024 for the M64 schedule)
- Sequence lengths or token counts: 2048 tokens per rank per layer; routings: uniform, one rank 2.5x hot, and a recorded production routing
- Parallelism: DP8 / EP8 on one host (TP1, PP1); EP16/EP32 across hosts is the next step (GIN) and was not measured
- Relevant shapes: hidden 5120, intermediate 2304, 384 experts (48 per rank at EP8), top-k 6, swiglu_limit 10, max_tokens_per_rank 2048; 8x sm_120 72 GB GPUs, 110 SMs, two PCIe Gen5 switches x 4 GPUs, 2x 400G RDMA NICs per switch
- Environment: output of `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` is attached as a comment on #6755 (flashinfer 399b6c1d source tree, torch 2.13 + NCCL 2.30.7, CUDA 13.3)

### Current workaround

We run the unfused path: DeepEP-style all-to-all with MXFP4 activations on dispatch, DeepGEMM `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` (FP4 x FP4) for both GEMMs, int8 combine, one copy per destination PCIe switch with in-switch partial-sum reduction. Its limitation is that communication and expert GEMMs are serial (about 1.97 ms + 1.93 ms per layer at this shape); a fused kernel could hide most of the smaller term, which is exactly what Cake does, but only if it does not double the bytes first.

### Impact

Throughput, Latency

### Acceptance criteria

- At E=384 / H=5120 / I=2304 / top-k 6, EP8, 2048 tokens per rank on an 8-GPU PCIe sm_120 host, the fused layer is not slower than the unfused MXFP4-activation path (3850 us/layer uniform, 4390 us/layer on recorded routing in our runs) and keeps the overlap gain measured against the same-precision unfused path (>= 10%).
- Per-card dispatch bytes at that shape ~24 MB/layer (MXFP4 rows) instead of ~46 MB; return bytes per route <= 5.3 KB.
- Correctness: passes `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_sm120_w4a8_cake_mega.py`-style oracle checks (rel L2 <= 2%) for the new activation/return formats, protocol_error stays 0, CUDA-graph replay bit-identical to eager, across EP4/8/16 and both row schedules.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- #6755: at this geometry the shipped build spills one register (STACK 16 B) and the backend refuses to load the workspace; the measurements above used `LOCAL_BYTES_LIMIT=16` in the test rig. That needs to be resolved first for any sm120 Cake variant to be usable on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- #6346 (the kernel), `kernel_src/sm120/cake_mxfp4_megamoe/README.md` (return codec, transport table, MOE_LSA_COPIERS).
- The SM100/SM107 `nvfp4_nvfp4` cutedsl families are the only W4A4 moe_ep kernels today; they use the NVFP4 recipe (e4m3 per-16 + per-tensor scale) rather than the MXFP4 checkpoint recipe (UE8M0 per-32) that the sm120 Cake weights already consume, so a W4A4 sm120 variant would ideally keep the MXFP4 recipe end to end.
- The dedupe/reduction scheme in (3) is what DeepEP's hybrid (two-hop) kernels do for NVLink+RDMA and what our PCIe variant does per switch; the per-pair transport table already carries the LSA/GIN topology needed to derive the groups.

### Timing or release need

_No response_

### Bug description
A planned `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(backend="cutlass")` accepts a page ID equal to the supplied KV pool size, a negative page ID, and a runtime KV pool shortened below an already planned page index. All three reach `cutlass_mla_paged_attention` without a clean rejection.

The expected behavior is a `ValueError` identifying the invalid KV page range before native dispatch. The reproduction intentionally intercepts the native entry for the invalid inputs: it confirms the validation gap without deliberately performing an out-of-bounds GPU access. It does not claim an observed illegal-memory-access crash. The finite, in-bounds control does execute the real kernel successfully.

This follows the MLA reject-or-correct slice of #3605. That slice currently describes page-ID values as trusted inputs. This dedicated issue tracks the missing validation and gives the CUTLASS-only quarantine a concrete re-enable signal, instead of citing the general quality tracker.

### Minimal reproduction
```python
import json
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch

from flashinfer.mla import BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper, MLAPlanMetadata


class ReachedNativeLaunch(Exception):
    pass


def stop_before_launch(*args, **kwargs):
    raise ReachedNativeLaunch


torch.manual_seed(0)
workspace = torch.empty(128 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
query = torch.randn(1, 128, 576, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
cache = torch.randn(2, 16, 576, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
results = []
for name, page_id, pool_size in (
    ("control", 1, 2),
    ("page_id_out_of_pool", 2, 2),
    ("page_id_negative", -1, 2),
    ("kv_pool_short", 1, 1),
):
    metadata = MLAPlanMetadata.csr(
        torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32),
        torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32),
        torch.tensor([page_id], dtype=torch.int32),
        torch.tensor([16], dtype=torch.int32),
    )
    wrapper = BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(workspace, backend="cutlass")
    wrapper.plan(
        metadata=metadata,
        num_heads=128,
        head_dim_ckv=512,
        head_dim_kpe=64,
        page_size=16,
        causal=False,
        sm_scale=192**-0.5,
        q_data_type=torch.bfloat16,
        kv_data_type=torch.bfloat16,
        query_layout="packed",
        kv_cache_layout="packed",
        lse_mode="none",
    )
    if name == "control":
        out = wrapper.run(query=query, kv_cache=cache)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        assert torch.isfinite(out).all()
        results.append(dict(case=name, result="finite output"))
        continue
    # Intercept the FFI entry so invalid memory is never accessed on the GPU.
    with patch.object(
        wrapper._planned_backend._cached_module,
        "cutlass_mla_paged_attention",
        stop_before_launch,
    ):
        try:
            wrapper.run(query=query, kv_cache=cache[:pool_size])
        except (ValueError, TypeError) as error:
            results.append(dict(case=name, result="rejected", error=str(error)))
        except ReachedNativeLaunch:
            results.append(dict(case=name, result="reached native launch"))
print(json.dumps(results))

```

### Results
```text
control: finite output
page_id_out_of_pool: reached native launch
page_id_negative: reached native launch
kv_pool_short: reached native launch
```

### Additional context
- Query: BF16 `[1,128,576]`; KV cache: BF16 `[2,16,576]`; CKV=512, KPE=64, Q=1, KV length=16, scale=`1/sqrt(192)`.
- The three invalid variants are isolated single-field changes after an in-bounds control.
- `cutlass_backend.py::run_from_wrapper` checks tensor shapes and planned page size, but does not compare the referenced page values with the runtime KV pool.
- A fix must preserve supported CUDA-graph metadata updates; caching only the initial page maximum can become stale when graph metadata changes.
- Related tracking scope: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3605#issuecomment-5590855985

items.title: [experimental/b12x] DSA indexer top-k determinism (tracking issue)
items.body:
**Owner:** @JMPSequeira

**Reason for experimental path:** The change lives entirely under `flashinfer/experimental/b12x/` (the b12x inference subsystem imported from the archived `local-inference-lab/b12x` repository, per that repo's migration guide and #5767). It fixes a nondeterminism bug in the DSA indexer's radix-select top-k: tied candidates were assigned output slots via shared-memory atomics (`_smem_xadd`) in nondeterministic thread order, so identical prompts selected jittering read plans across runs — observed as a 27–31% coherence-flake rate on a 32K verbatim-recall canary under a production serving profile (TP2+DCP2, MTP3, GLM-5.3-Flash, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). The fix perturbs the radix-select key by `candidate_index * 2^-24` (output scores untouched), making tie resolution deterministic without changing the selected score set.

**Graduation plan:** Bug-level determinism fix, not a new backend surface; propose graduating with the next regular b12x experimental release once the experimental CI lane validates the two determinism test files. Can also be folded into any pending b12x port PR as a prerequisite.

Port PR to follow: port of archived `local-inference-lab/b12x` commit `59548d5429a59bc869aa7d61cfef9a8486114171`, authorship preserved.

items.title: [Performance] XQA generic launcher on SM12x: the split leaves a near-empty second wave and over-splits short sequences
items.body:
On SM12x every non-MLA XQA decode runs the generic launcher, `launchMHAFlashInfer` in `csrc/xqa/mha.cu` (the SM90 FP8 kernel is capability 9 only), which sets `nbSubSeqPerSeq = min(max(1, SMs / (batch * nbKHeads)), divUp(maxSeqLen, 256))` at one CTA per SM. Two cases lose on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (188 SMs; FlashInfer 0.7.2, FP8 KV, page 16, vLLM's `xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` calls, KV larger than L2, CUDA-graph timing, 5 rounds).

When batch x KV heads is just above the SM count, the second wave is nearly empty: Qwen3-4B (8 KV heads) at batch 24 is 192 CTAs, 4 of them in a second wave, and split 6 is 12 to 13% faster from 4K to 64K tokens (level at 1K). Short sequences are over-split, because the length bound is the block-table width (max_model_len in vLLM): with a 64K table, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (2 KV heads) at batch 1 runs split 94, and split 4 is 2.5x faster at 1K tokens, split 16 2.1x at 4K.

End to end on vLLM main `153a17166e` (Qwen3-4B, FP8 KV, 16K context), forcing only batch 24 to split 6 cuts decode ITL from 31.4 to 28.5 ms over four interleaved boots, with batch 8 and 1 unchanged.

vLLM captures one decode graph per batch size, so a context-blind rule trades short contexts against long ones (split 8 at batch 32 is 35% slower at 1K). #5998 traced its SM90 case to this launcher, and #4904's `computeNbSubSeqPerSeq` is the natural template, its `max_kv_len` bound helping callers that know the length at launch. Would a split that changes only when the last wave is partial be acceptable here? I have the sweep and can open a PR.

cc @bkryu

items.title: [Feature]: prims_ts dense paged decode: allow FP8-E4M3 Q/KV with BF16 output
items.body:
### Before submitting - [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet. ### Problem The prims_ts dense paged decode path accepts FP8-E4M3 Q with FP8-E4M3 K/V only when the output is FP16 or FP8. BF16 output is rejected. Checked on **v0.7.1** and **v0.7.2** (`d84335d`); `main` has the same code. ``` NotImplementedError: attention-ts decode supports FP16->FP16, BF16->BF16, FP8-E4M3->FP16, and FP8-E4M3->FP8-E4M3; BF16 Q + FP8 K/V, BF16/FP8-E4M3 Q + NVFP4 K/V, and BF16 Q/K + FP8 V; got Q_torch.float8_e4m3fn_K_torch.float8_e4m3fn_V_torch.float8_e4m3fn->torch.bfloat16 ``` Two checks restrict FP8 Q → BF16 output to the QToken-KvBlock sparse route (links are to v0.7.2): 1. [`_validate_dtype_pair`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L695-L748) allows it only with `allow_fp8_bf16_output=True`. Only the sparse route sets that flag: [`allow_fp8_bf16_output=use_q_token_kv_block_sparse_route`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L3431-L3437), with `use_q_token_kv_block_sparse_route=True` passed only from `q_token_kv_block_sparse_metadata.py`. Every dense entry point rejects BF16: | dense entry point | where it rejects FP8 Q/KV → BF16 | |---|---| | `BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.plan` | [decode.py:3875](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L3875), **only when `validate=True`** | | `batch_decode_with_paged_kv_cache` (no `workspace_buffer`) | `get_prims_ts_batch_decode_workspace_size`, [decode.py:2054](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L2054) | | `prepare_prims_ts_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` | `_prepare_prims_ts_batch_decode_plan(use_q_token_kv_block_sparse_route=False)`, [decode.py:3431](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/decode.py#L3431-L3437) | 2. [`FmhaDecodeConfig.supports_reduction_dtypes`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.2/flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/kernels/fmha_decode/fmha_decode_config.py#L1275-L1290) returns False for FP8 Q → BF16 output unless `uses_q_token_kv_block_sparse_page_route` is set. This check doesn't raise. When it fails, the automatic policy drops the cluster SMEM reduction. So a caller whose activations are BF16 has to request FP16 and run a separate FP16 → BF16 cast after every attention call. **Results.** GB300, B=4, 4 query tokens per request, 16 Q heads, 1 KV head, head_dim 128, page 128, KV length 4096, dense mask. Each mode ran in a fresh process, because `_resolve_decode_launch_spec` is `functools.cache`d. v0.7.1 and v0.7.2 give identical numbers. | mode | planned config | rel. error vs FP32 ref | rel. diff vs FP16 output | time (CUDA-graph replay, CUDA events, warm L2) | |---|---|--:|--:|--:| | FP16 output (supported today) | `splits_kv=6`, cluster SMEM reduction | 2.504e-2 | — | | | FP16 output + cast to BF16 (current workaround) | | | | 10.42 µs | | BF16 output, `plan(validate=False)`, no patch (`--no-validate`) | `splits_kv=8`, no cluster SMEM reduction | 2.523e-2 | 2.03e-2 | 7.96 µs | | BF16 output, only `_validate_dtype_pair` relaxed (`--relax-pair-only`) | `splits_kv=8`, no cluster SMEM reduction | 2.523e-2 | 2.03e-2 | 7.96 µs | | BF16 output, both checks relaxed (`--relax`) | `splits_kv=6`, cluster SMEM reduction | 2.513e-2 | 2.36e-3 | **7.35 µs** | - **Accuracy:** every BF16 row has the same error vs the FP32 reference as FP16 output, about 2.5e-2. That error comes from the FP8 inputs. - **Both checks relaxed:** the BF16 plan matches the FP16 plan, and the output differs from FP16 output only by BF16 rounding (2.4e-3). It takes 7.35 µs vs 10.42 µs for the workaround. - **`validate=False` is inconsistent:** `BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.plan(validate=False)` already builds and runs FP8 → BF16 with no patch. The dtype check is skipped, but `supports_reduction_dtypes` still fails, so the policy falls back to 8 splits without the cluster SMEM reduction. On this entry point the dtype check only applies under `validate=True`, and with `validate=False` the reduction check quietly gives a slower plan. Relaxing only `_validate_dtype_pair` gives the same result, so both checks need to change together. - **Wider sweep:** at B = 1–64, with the same heads, page size, KV length and timing method, relaxing both checks saved 3.3–3.9 µs per call against FP16 output + cast. The difference from FP16 output stayed at 1.4e-3 to 2.8e-3. **Related:** #5720 relaxes the same two checks for FP8 Q with NVFP4 K/V → BF16 on the dense route. It also adds `test_attention_ts_decode_fp8_kv_bf16_output_remains_route_scoped`, which asserts that FP8 K/V → BF16 stays rejected outside the sparse route. If that restriction is deliberate, could you share the reason? At this shape, the dense kernels pick the same plan and give the same accuracy as with FP16 output once both checks are relaxed.
Minimal reproduction (repro_fp8_bf16_out.py) ```python """prims_ts dense paged decode: FP8-E4M3 Q/KV -> BF16 output is rejected. python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py # FP16 output works, BF16 raises python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --relax # relax both dtype gates python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --relax-pair-only # relax _validate_dtype_pair only python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --no-validate # plan(validate=False), no patch """ import argparse import functools import torch from flashinfer.attention.prims_ts import BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper B, SQ, HQ, HKV, D, PAGE, KV_LEN = 4, 4, 16, 1, 128, 128, 4096 FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn def relax_gates(reduction=True): import flashinfer.attention.prims_ts.decode as dec from flashinfer.attention.prims_ts.kernels.fmha_decode import ( fmha_decode_config as cfg, ) validate = dec._validate_dtype_pair @functools.wraps(validate) def validate_relaxed(*args, **kwargs): kwargs["allow_fp8_bf16_output"] = True return validate(*args, **kwargs) dec._validate_dtype_pair = validate_relaxed if not reduction: return reduction_ok = cfg.FmhaDecodeConfig.supports_reduction_dtypes.fget cfg.FmhaDecodeConfig.supports_reduction_dtypes = property( lambda c: reduction_ok(c) or (c.q_dtype == cfg.Float8E4M3FN and c.out_dtype == cfg.BFloat16) ) def make_inputs(): torch.manual_seed(0) pages = KV_LEN // PAGE q = torch.randn(B, SQ, HQ, D, device="cuda").to(FP8) k = (0.5 * torch.randn(B * pages, HKV, PAGE, D, device="cuda")).to(FP8) v = (0.5 * torch.randn(B * pages, HKV, PAGE, D, device="cuda")).to(FP8) block_tables = torch.arange(B * pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") seq_lens = torch.full((B,), KV_LEN, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") return q, k, v, block_tables.view(B, pages), seq_lens def reference(q, k, v, block_tables): def gather(x): # [pages, HKV, PAGE, D] -> [B, HQ, KV_LEN, D] x = x.float()[block_tables].permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshape(B, HKV, -1, D) return x.repeat_interleave(HQ // HKV, dim=1) s = q.float().transpose(1, 2) @ gather(k).transpose(-1, -2) * D**-0.5 return (s.softmax(-1) @ gather(v)).transpose(1, 2) # [B, SQ, HQ, D] def make_call(out_dtype, q, k, v, block_tables, seq_lens, validate=True): wrapper = BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper(kv_layout="HND") wrapper.plan( "cuda", B, HQ, HKV, D, PAGE, KV_LEN, max_seq_len_q=SQ, q_data_type=FP8, kv_data_type=FP8, o_data_type=out_dtype, mask_type="dense", validate=validate, ) policy = dict(wrapper._plan_state.policy) print(f" {out_dtype} plan: " + ", ".join( f"{key}={policy[key]}" for key in ("splits_kv", "use_cluster_smem_reduction"))) out = torch.empty(B, SQ, HQ, D, dtype=out_dtype, device="cuda") kwargs = dict(seq_lens=seq_lens, block_tables=block_tables, bmm1_scale=D**-0.5, out=out) wrapper.run(q, (k, v), **kwargs) return out, lambda: wrapper.run(q, (k, v), validate=False, **kwargs) def rel_err(x, ref): return ((x.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item() def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--relax", action="store_true") parser.add_argument("--relax-pair-only", action="store_true") parser.add_argument("--no-validate", action="store_true") args = parser.parse_args() if args.relax or args.relax_pair_only: relax_gates(reduction=not args.relax_pair_only) inputs = make_inputs() ref = reference(*inputs[:4]) out16, run16 = make_call(torch.float16, *inputs) print(f"FP8 Q/KV -> FP16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref {rel_err(out16, ref):.3e}") try: out_bf16, run_bf16 = make_call(torch.bfloat16, *inputs, validate=not args.no_validate) except NotImplementedError as e: print(f"FP8 Q/KV -> BF16 out: NotImplementedError: {e}") return print(f"FP8 Q/KV -> BF16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref {rel_err(out_bf16, ref):.3e}, " f"vs FP16 out {rel_err(out_bf16, out16.float()):.3e}") from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cudagraph def median_us(fn): t = sorted(bench_gpu_time_with_cudagraph(fn, cold_l2_cache=False)) return t[len(t) // 2] * 1e3 cast = torch.empty_like(out_bf16) print(f"FP16 out + cast to BF16: {median_us(lambda: (run16(), cast.copy_(out16))):.2f} us") print(f"BF16 out: {median_us(run_bf16):.2f} us") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Output on GB300 with v0.7.2 (FlashInfer warnings removed; v0.7.1 prints the same): ``` $ python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py torch.float16 plan: splits_kv=6, use_cluster_smem_reduction=True FP8 Q/KV -> FP16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.504e-02 FP8 Q/KV -> BF16 out: NotImplementedError: attention-ts decode supports FP16->FP16, BF16->BF16, FP8-E4M3->FP16, and FP8-E4M3->FP8-E4M3; BF16 Q + FP8 K/V, BF16/FP8-E4M3 Q + NVFP4 K/V, and BF16 Q/K + FP8 V; got Q_torch.float8_e4m3fn_K_torch.float8_e4m3fn_V_torch.float8_e4m3fn->torch.bfloat16 $ python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --no-validate torch.float16 plan: splits_kv=6, use_cluster_smem_reduction=True FP8 Q/KV -> FP16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.504e-02 torch.bfloat16 plan: splits_kv=8, use_cluster_smem_reduction=False FP8 Q/KV -> BF16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.523e-02, vs FP16 out 2.034e-02 FP16 out + cast to BF16: 10.42 us BF16 out: 7.96 us $ python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --relax-pair-only torch.float16 plan: splits_kv=6, use_cluster_smem_reduction=True FP8 Q/KV -> FP16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.504e-02 torch.bfloat16 plan: splits_kv=8, use_cluster_smem_reduction=False FP8 Q/KV -> BF16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.523e-02, vs FP16 out 2.034e-02 FP16 out + cast to BF16: 10.42 us BF16 out: 7.96 us $ python repro_fp8_bf16_out.py --relax torch.float16 plan: splits_kv=6, use_cluster_smem_reduction=True FP8 Q/KV -> FP16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.504e-02 torch.bfloat16 plan: splits_kv=6, use_cluster_smem_reduction=True FP8 Q/KV -> BF16 out: rel err vs FP32 ref 2.513e-02, vs FP16 out 2.362e-03 FP16 out + cast to BF16: 10.42 us BF16 out: 7.35 us ```
### Requested outcome Support FP8-E4M3 Q + FP8-E4M3 K/V → BF16 output on the dense prims_ts paged decode path, through all dense entry points, with split-KV on and off. The BF16 plan should get the same split/reduction policy as the FP16-output plan, so callers can write BF16 directly instead of writing FP16 and casting. ### Target hardware SM103 (B300, GB300) ### Inference engine Not applicable ### Workload and configuration - Data type and quantization: FP8-E4M3 Q, FP8-E4M3 K/V (unit scales), BF16 output wanted - Batch size or request concurrency: 1–64 requests - Sequence lengths or token counts: 4 query tokens per request (fixed, `max_seq_len_q=4`), KV length 4096 - Parallelism: n/a (single-GPU kernel) - Relevant shapes: 16 Q heads, 1 KV head, head_dim 128, page_size 128, HND layout, `mask_type="dense"` - Environment: GB300 (SM103), driver 610.43.02, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.7.1 and 0.7.2, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0 ### Current workaround Request FP16 output and copy it into a BF16 buffer after every call. That adds a kernel launch and a round trip through memory: 10.42 µs vs 7.35 µs at the shape above. `plan(validate=False)` with BF16 output runs, but it bypasses a check the library treats as a hard restriction, and it gets the slower plan without the cluster reduction (7.96 µs). ### Impact Latency ### Acceptance criteria - `BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.plan`, `batch_decode_with_paged_kv_cache`, `prepare_prims_ts_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` and `get_prims_ts_batch_decode_workspace_size` accept FP8 Q/KV → BF16 output, with `split_kv=True` and `split_kv=False`, for dense and causal masks. - The BF16 output matches the FP16-output result to within BF16 rounding (2.4e-3 relative in the repro). - The BF16-output plan gets the same `splits_kv` / `use_cluster_smem_reduction` as the FP16-output plan and runs in about the same time. ### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope Probably small in scope: - In `_validate_dtype_pair`, allow BF16 output for FP8 Q with FP8 K/V on the dense route. #5720 does the same for NVFP4 K/V by checking `k_dtype == torch.uint8`. - In `supports_reduction_dtypes`, drop the `uses_q_token_kv_block_sparse_page_route` condition from the BF16 case. #5720 does this for `use_nvfp4_kv`. - Add FP8 → BF16 cases to the existing prims_ts decode tests.

## Summary

At Nemotron-3-Ultra's TP4 shard geometry (nheads 64, head_dim 64, d_state 128,
ngroups 2), FlashInfer's SSD chunked-prefill kernel runs **1.34–1.38x behind vLLM's
in-tree Triton chunk-scan on all 66 captured classes**. The verdict is
shard-geometry-sensitive: at the TP2 shard (nheads 128) FI is **1.19x ahead** on all
351 classes — so the gap is specific to the narrower per-rank head count, not the op.
Separately, FlashInfer ships no causal-conv1d kernel at any version we tested, so the
conv stage of the Mamba2 block always stays on the framework kernel even where FI
wins the SSM stage.

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
  (measured at SSM-stage granularity; conv stage excluded for every candidate)
- Shapes from live serving of the published Nemotron-3-Ultra GB300 recipes
  (vLLM TP4 and SGLang TP2 legs)

## Exact call parameters

SSD chunked prefill: `nheads=64`, `head_dim=64`, `d_state=128`, `ngroups=2`,
`chunk_size=128`, `batch=1` varlen (T = total tokens in the call), bf16
activations. TP2 contrast rows use `nheads=128`, all else equal.

## Measurements — TP4 shard: nheads 64, head_dim 64, d_state 128, ngroups 2 (µs)

| chunk tokens | FI `ssd` | vLLM Triton chunk-scan | FI behind |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8480 | 449.7 | 336.8 | 1.34x |
| 16536–16960 | 862.7–878.8 | 630.5–644.9 | 1.36–1.38x |
| 25440 | 1307.8 | 951.0 | 1.38x |

Contrast, TP2 shard (nheads 128, same op): FI 1.19x ahead GPU-time-weighted, all
classes. Decode (selective-state-update) is competitive at both shards and ahead at
the speculative q=6 regime.

## Ask

1. Close the SSD chunk-scan gap at the 64-head shard (tiling for the half-width
   head count looks like the lever, given the 128-head win).
2. Ship a causal-conv1d kernel so the Mamba2 block can run FI end-to-end; today the
   conv stage forces a framework-kernel dependency regardless of SSM-stage wins.

## Related

items.title: [Perf][SM103] GQA fp8 decode: the direct trtllm-gen entry runs ~1.15x behind FI's own BatchDecode wrapper on the same shapes
items.body:
## Summary

On captured GQA decode traffic (16 q-heads / 1 kv-head per rank, head_dim 128,
fp8 KV), the **direct** trtllm-gen decode entry — the path vLLM integrates — is
**~1.15x behind FlashInfer's own `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`**
(GPU-time-weighted; cute-dsl backend at long KV, trtllm-gen-via-wrapper at short
KV). The wrapper forms also beat the best non-FI rival (vLLM's FA fp8) on most of
the traffic, so this within-FI gap is the difference between FI winning and losing
the cell as integrated. We see the same direct-vs-wrapper gap on two different
models' serves (Nemotron-3-Ultra and MiniMax-M3, both vLLM).

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
- Shapes + weights from live serving of the published Nemotron-3-Ultra vLLM GB300
  recipe (TP4; speculative decode q=6 plus q=1 traffic)

## Exact call parameters

GQA paged decode: `num_q_heads=16`, `num_kv_heads=1`, `head_dim=128`,
q and KV `float8_e4m3fn`, paged KV with `page_size=32`, bf16 output;
`q_len=1` rows below (the serve also runs q_len=6 speculative verify — see ask 2).

## Measurements — q=1, 16/1 heads, head_dim 128, fp8 KV (µs, top classes by GPU time)

| batch | kv_len | direct trtllm-gen | wrapper (best backend) | vLLM FA fp8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 65536 | 21.6 | 18.8 (cute-dsl) | 22.6 |
| 1 | 131072 | 27.8 | 23.3 (cute-dsl) | 26.1 |
| 1 | 262144 | 32.5 | 27.9 (cute-dsl) | 32.5 |
| 2 | 131072 | 24.9 | 22.9 (cute-dsl) | 27.9 |
| 2 | 262144 | 35.3 | 32.9 (cute-dsl) | 38.8 |
| 1 | 8192 | 8.2 | 6.9 (trtllm-gen) | 14.0 |
| 2 | 4096 | 7.2 | 6.0 (trtllm-gen) | 11.3 |

Note the short-KV rows: even *trtllm-gen itself* is faster through the wrapper than
through the direct entry, so part of the gap is entry-point overhead/config rather
than kernel choice.

## Why this is a FlashInfer issue, not an integration nit

The obvious rejoinder — "vLLM should just call the wrapper" — doesn't hold yet: at
the serve's dominant q=6 speculative-verify traffic, the wrapper forms are **not
eligible at all** at this geometry, so the direct entry is the only FI decode path
that covers the whole regime, and an integration reasonably wants one
CUDA-graphable decode path rather than a per-q_len API switch. Given FI's current
surface, vLLM's pick is the correct one — and FI loses the cell with it. Both
fixes live in FlashInfer:

## Ask

1. Extend the wrapper/cute-dsl decode eligibility to q_len > 1 (speculative verify,
   q=6 here) at this head geometry — this is what unblocks integrations from using
   the fast forms at all.
2. Bring the direct trtllm-gen decode entry to parity with the wrapper (or route it
   through the same backend selection): the short-KV rows above show the *same
   backend* running faster through the wrapper, so the overhead is in the entry
   point itself, and fixing it speeds up every existing integration with no
   framework change.

items.title: [Perf][SM103] sparse MLA decode: bf16-dense-KV ABI doubles KV bytes vs FlashMLA's packed pages; mid-batch q=6 verify regression (B=3–12)
items.body:
## Summary

On DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse MLA (top-k 512, real captured indexer selections),
FlashInfer's SM103 path requires a **bf16 dense KV cache**, while FlashMLA reads a
584-byte/token packed fp8 page — ~2x KV bytes per decode step for FI. On the
call-count-weighted view over 3,819 real selections FlashMLA comes out ~1.2x ahead
(FI wins the expensive full-length prefills and net device time, so the verdict is
genuinely split). Inside the decode family there is a clean, shape-local regression:
at the production verify width (q=6, table width 640), FI is **1.5–1.6x ahead at
batch 1–2, then 1.04–1.43x behind for batch 3–12**, then ahead again at 13+.
The serving integration also pays a per-step index repack feeding the FI call
(~8% of FI attention time), which the packed-page rivals do not need.

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5; rival: FlashMLA (vLLM build)
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
- Workloads: real indexer selections captured from live serving of the published
  DeepSeek-V4.1 GB300 recipes and replayed verbatim (grid-synthetic selection
  patterns overstate FI's cost ~2x, so only real selections are used)

## Exact call parameters

Sparse MLA decode: `num_q_heads=16`, `head_dim=512` (+64 RoPE), q_len 6 per
sequence (speculative verify), selection table width 640 (top-k 512 + sliding
window 128), real captured per-sequence KV lengths 31k-108k; FI reads a bf16
dense KV pool (its SM103 ABI), FlashMLA reads its packed 584 B/token fp8 pages —
same selections replayed for both.

## Measurements — q=6 verify decode, table width 640 (µs)

| batch | FlashMLA | FI (trtllm-gen) | verdict |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 22.2 | 13.5 | FI 1.64x ahead |
| 2 | 22.2 | 15.2 | FI 1.46x ahead |
| 3 | 22.2 | 23.1 | FI 1.04x behind |
| 6 | 22.3 | 23.9 | FI 1.07x behind |
| 9 | 22.5 | 30.9 | FI 1.37x behind |
| 12 | 22.7 | 32.6 | FI 1.43x behind |
| 13 | 22.8 | 19.1 | FI 1.19x ahead |

FlashMLA is nearly flat in batch; FI's cost ramps from B=3 and drops back at B=13 —
it looks like a tiling/scheduling boundary. At the narrow table width (128) FI is
ahead across the board (the new `cake` backend takes several small-B classes).

## Ask

1. An fp8-packed KV page format for SM103 sparse MLA (it exists on SM120 only
   today) — the 2x KV-byte handicap is structural, and vLLM already defines a
   compatible 352-byte nvfp4 layout (#5716) and a 584-byte fp8 layout.
2. Fix the B=3–12 ramp at q=6/W=640 (the production verify regime: its weight is
   concentrated exactly at B=3–12 in our captures).

## Related

- #6301 (DSv4/4.1 sparse attention backend support, SM100/103/107)
- #5716 (nvfp4_ds_mla compressed KV layout)

items.title: [Perf][SM103] MSA sparse prefill: runtime scales with prefix length instead of queries x top-k — ~18 ms flat at a 64K prefix, 113x behind Triton on chunk-append
items.body:
## Summary

On MiniMax-M3's MSA sparse prefill (top-k 16 blocks of 128, fp8-e4m3 KV),
FlashInfer's MSA prefill kernel costs **~17.9 ms whenever the attended prefix is
65536 tokens — regardless of how many queries the call carries** (512 or 16384).
With top-k sparsity each query touches at most 16x128 = 2048 KV positions, so a
512-query call has no business costing milliseconds: the in-tree Triton sparse
kernel does the same call in 157 µs (**113x**). On fresh sequences (prefix 0) the
same FI kernel is fine — it *beats* that Triton kernel 1.6–2.8x at large q — so the
pathology is specifically whatever work scales with prefix length.

Related route-level finding: FI's E4M3-KV route is a median ~5.9x slower than FI's
own bf16-KV route on identical shapes, and the fp8 cache is what this model serves.

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5 (identical times at both FI
  versions we ran; the serve-pinned 0.6.x wheels ship no msa_ops at all)
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
- Shapes from live-serve captures of the published MiniMax-M3 GB300 recipes

## Exact call parameters

MSA sparse prefill: `num_q_heads=16`, `num_kv_heads=1`, `head_dim=128`, top-k 16,
`block_size=128`, indexer 1 head x 128 dim, KV `float8_e4m3fn`, `batch=1` varlen.
Rows vary `per_seq_q` (queries in the call) and `prefix_len` (already-cached
tokens the selection runs over).

## Measurements (µs)

| per_seq_q | prefix_len | FI msa prefill | in-tree Triton sparse | FI vs Triton |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8 | 0 | 76.8 | 13.2 | 5.8x behind |
| 8192 | 0 | 1247.3 | 3481.6 | **2.8x ahead** |
| 16384 | 0 | 2358.9 | 3708.4 | **1.6x ahead** |
| 8 | 65536 | 17842.9 | 157.3 | **113x behind** |
| 8192 | 65536 | 16996.6 | 3960.3 | 4.3x behind |
| 16384 | 65536 | 18226.8 | 3962.1 | 4.6x behind |

The FI column at prefix 65536 is flat (~17–18 ms) across a 2048x range of query
counts. (A second rival, the SGLang fused sparse FMHA, leads everything at large q
— 713 µs at the heaviest row — but the prefix-flat behavior is the FI-side bug.)

## Ask

1. Make MSA prefill cost scale with queries x top-k, not prefix length — whatever
   per-call work walks the full prefix (selection re-processing, metadata build,
   or a dense pass) dominates the chunk-append regime that chunked prefill runs.
2. Close the E4M3-KV vs bf16-KV route gap (median ~5.9x on identical shapes) —
   the fp8 cache regime is the one production uses.

## Related

- #6020 (packed-FP8 MSA sparse decode for MiniMax-M3, SM100/SM103 — experimental)

items.title: [Perf/Feature] KDA decode: recurrent path 4.2–5.7x behind vendored Triton at the 64-head geometry; fused ops reject H=64; fp32 state crashes instead of raising
items.body:
## Summary

Three stacked problems keep FlashInfer's KDA family out of GLM-5.3 serving:

1. **Perf:** at GLM-5.3's per-rank decode geometry (H=64, T=1), FI's recurrent KDA
   (`cute-dsl`, run with its documented bf16 state) is **4.2–5.7x behind** the
   frameworks' kernels (vLLM's vendored fla Triton / FlashKDA) at every batch size.
2. **Eligibility:** FI's *fused* KDA decode ops reject the 64-head count outright,
   so the fast path never applies at this geometry (it wins at the Kimi-K3 head
   counts, where FI leads 1.13x decode / 1.22x chunk-prefill).
3. **Contract:** both serving frameworks keep **fp32** KDA state pools. Feeding
   fp32 state to FI's decode produces a misleading crash signature instead of a
   dtype error, which is part of why no framework integrates the FI family at all
   (four distinct non-FI KDA implementations ship across vLLM/SGLang today).

## Environment

- NVIDIA GB300 (SM103); CUDA 13.0; FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5
- Timing: CUPTI, 20 interleaved rounds, SM clock locked 2070 MHz, fp64 gates
- Geometry from the published GLM-5.3 GB300 recipes (TP2/TP4 shards → H=64/rank)

## Exact call parameters

KDA recurrent decode: `num_heads=64`, `num_v_heads=64`, `d_k=128`, `d_v=128`,
`T=1` token per sequence, bf16 q/k/v with bf16 recurrent state (FI's documented
contract; the frameworks hold fp32 state). Batch varies below.

## Measurements — H=64, T=1 decode step (µs)

| batch | vLLM recurrent (fla Triton) | FlashKDA packed | FI recurrent (cute-dsl) | FI behind |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.6 | 3.5 | 20.0 | 5.7x |
| 8 | 14.0 | 15.5 | 47.3 | 3.4x |
| 32 | 44.1 | 50.7 | 183.0 | 4.2x |
| 128 | 167.9 | 186.0 | 771.4 | 4.6x |

(`fi_auto` matches `cute-dsl` within noise, so this is the best FI has at H=64.)

## Ask

1. Whitelist H=64 in the fused KDA decode ops (or document why it is excluded) —
   GLM-5.3's shard geometry lands exactly there.
2. Make the recurrent path competitive at H=64/T=1, or route it to the fused
   kernels once (1) lands.
3. Raise a clear dtype error on fp32 decode state instead of crashing; better,
   accept fp32 state — it is what both frameworks' state pools hold, and it is the
   single biggest adoption blocker for the FI KDA family even where FI already wins
   (Kimi-K3 geometry).

## Related
